name: Lip-Bu Tan

career.organization: EDS Nuclear; ECHO Energy; Chappell & Co.
career.title: Engineering and management roles; Vice President at Chappell & Co.

background_rationale: Built his career as a venture capitalist after founding Walden International in 1987, then applied that tech-investing base to lead Cadence Design Systems and Intel.

notable.summary: Intel confirmed it would cut nearly 24,000 jobs, about 15% of its workforce, by the end of 2025 as part of a restructuring under Tan.

After President Trump called for his resignation over his China ties, Tan wrote to Intel employees that the United States had been his home for more than 40 years and that he was engaging with the administration.
Intel agreed to an $8.9 billion investment by the U.S. government for a 9.9% passive stake, funded largely by previously awarded CHIPS Act grants.
Intel and Nvidia announced a partnership to co-develop data-center and PC products, with Nvidia investing $5 billion in Intel common stock.

personal_story.hook: Lip-Bu Tan left MIT's nuclear engineering PhD program after Three Mile Island and later became Intel's CEO.
personal_story.summary: Tan was born in 1959 in Muar, in what is now Malaysia, the youngest of five children; his father edited a major Chinese-language newspaper and his mother worked at Nanyang University. Among high-achieving siblings, he once called himself "kind of a drop out." After a physics degree from Nanyang University, he entered MIT's nuclear engineering doctoral program, earning a master's but withdrawing after the 1979 Three Mile Island accident because he feared nuclear power had no future in the U.S. He earned an MBA in San Francisco, worked briefly in engineering, and in 1987, the year he became a U.S. citizen, founded the venture firm Walden International with a roughly $3 million first fund. Decades of chip-industry investing led to a turnaround run as Cadence CEO and, in March 2025, the top job at Intel.
